owner_rules: Done means ALL evidence: implemented as specified (task id), a test that FAILED before and passes now, suites green, measured number vs target, docs regenerated, committed AND pushed to main.

Honest reporting: TASK-ID | status | commit | tests | measured vs target | missing.
The verifier never controls its own trust boundary: contract, evidence and gate records change only through the owner deploy key.
Heuristic checks are one layer, never a boundary; say so in every receipt and page.

tasks.title: A contract change commits only with the owner's approval marker for its exact bytes
tasks.description: The pre-commit hook (src/index.mjs hookPreCommit, src/contract.mjs weakenings) keeps refusing a staged proofline.json whose weakenings against HEAD are not empty. The one path through it is an approval marker written by the owner: a file named <approvals directory>/<sha256 hex of the staged proofline.json bytes>. The approvals directory is set per clone with `proofline init --approvals <dir>` (re-runnable) and kept in .proofline/config.json, which is never committed; with no directory configured every contract change is refused. Red on the parent: with the marker present for a changed criterion command, `proofline hook pre-commit` still refuses, because no marker logic exists.

tasks.title: receipt command, contract mode, signed with agentkey
tasks.description: External dependency: @optitransfer/agentkey on npm (0.1.0 under latest since 2026-10-16); if absent report BLOCKED. The dependency is the scoped name, pinned exactly; the unscoped npm name agentkey belongs to a third party and never appears in package.json or in an import. agentkey is loaded where a receipt is signed, so a missing key or a load failure yields an L0 receipt with the reason, never a crash. Export buildReceipt(opts) from src/receipt.mjs and call it from bin/proofline.mjs. New command `proofline receipt <TASK> [--role <role>] [--base <sha>] [--out <path>]`. Runs verify for the task and builds the predicate https://proofline.dev/receipt/v1 with the fields (level, producer, base, task, tests{changed, red_on_base{ran,failed,output_sha256}, green_on_head{ran,passed,output_sha256}}, suite{command,exit,count,duration_ms}, metrics[], scope{allowed,changed,pass}, forbidden{findings,pass}, claims{reported,reconciled}, agent{role,kid,run_id,model?,trace?}, memory?, timestamps). Subject: {name: "git+<remote url>@<ref>", digest:{gitCommit, gitTree}}. Signs with agentkey signDSSE for the role (default PROOFLINE_AGENT_ROLE, else level L0 unsigned). Writes .proofline/receipts/<sha7>.json (the envelope); init already ignores .proofline/ (src/index.mjs:24), and `proofline init --keep-receipts` adds the negation `!.proofline/receipts/` for teams that commit them. Subject name: "git+<remote url>@<ref>" for public repositories, "<ref>" with the repository only in predicate.repository for private ones. Subject binding rules every verifier applies: subject.gitCommit must equal the head being judged and predicate.base.gitCommit the base; a tree-only match marks base-relative fields (red_on_base, scope) unverified unless recomputed. tests.red_on_base and green_on_head carry attempts; suite carries reruns. Red means exit != 0 on base (a module-not-found counts), stated in docs. schema/receipt-v1.json is a JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) for the predicate; the command validates against it before signing. Every boolean has a sibling `ran`.

tasks.title: The pre-push hook gates each commit being pushed, at that commit
tasks.description: The hook reads the local sha on each stdin line git hands it, derives the task id from the (TASK-ID) suffix of that commit's subject (or the Proofline-Task trailer when present), and gates that task at that sha in a temporary worktree. The base is the most recent task_started record for the task, else the commit's parent, so a later start re-pins it. A worktree with no evidence still gates, a worktree with stale evidence cannot block a clean commit, and pushing the first commit of a chain gates that commit, not the branch tip. Refuses when any gated task is not PASS; prints the base it used in every refusal. Closes the three findings of 2026-10-16: the hook gated HEAD (issue 21), the base could not be re-pinned (issue 22), an evidence-free worktree passed (issue 23).

tasks.title: An active task ends when it lands; the hook gates the task of the commit being pushed
tasks.description: Finding of 2026-10-16: .proofline/active kept naming a task after that task's commits were on main, so the pre-push hook gated the finished task against every later branch (its scope criterion failed on the later task's files) and refused pushes that had nothing to do with it. Fix: `next`, `verify` and the hooks treat an active task as ended once its head is an ancestor of origin/main (or its pushed criterion has a PASS record), clear the file and say so; the hook derives the task to gate from the commits being pushed ((TASK-ID) subject suffix or the Proofline-Task trailer) and falls back to the active task only for a commit that names none; a landed task is never gated. The README's hook section states which task a push is gated on. Bootstrap: until the first task_started record exists, a push whose commits name no task passes with the next command printed, so the owner can push init, the baseline and the approved contract; from the first start on, every push names its task or is refused. The demo in examples/ follows the same order.

tasks.title: The pre-push hook gates only commits the server does not already hold
tasks.description: Finding of 2026-10-16 (issue 31): sending a branch that was rebased onto a newer main made the sent range every commit not on the remote branch, which included tasks already landed on main, so the hook re-gated them and refused the send. If the server cannot be read, the hook gates every commit in the push range (fail closed).

tasks.title: Receipt note in hivevault's format, sent raw
tasks.description: Finding of 2026-10-16 (proofline issue 37; programme round trip I4 and I7): hivevault refuses the note proofline writes, written directly and through a live daemon. The format belongs to hivevault: HV-02 at hivevault 7602907f4449e76a04fc611d4b6c33cd56af9c9f, implemented by its cli/receipts.mjs receiptNote. This task does not restate that format; it reproduces it. The fixture is the spec: test/fixtures/hivevault-receipt-note.md and test/fixtures/hivevault-receipt-note.inputs.json, made by hivevault's own receiptNote and handed over by the lead, the inputs file naming `from` (the hivevault path and commit) and the sha256 of cli/receipts.mjs at that commit. src/vault.mjs receiptNote reproduces the fixture byte for byte from its inputs. What proofline computes itself: the path uses the head commit's first seven hex characters; agent.kid equals envelope.signatures[0].keyid; subject.pr is 0 for a local run with no pull request; an L0 receipt gets no note (hivevault refuses an unsigned envelope) and the writer says so on stderr. writeReceiptNote sends {raw, origin, commit_message} on PUT /v1/notes/<path>, never a frontmatter object (stored one line per key, measured: subject: [object Object]). No run-time import of hivevault. test/vault_link.test.mjs is the one existing test whose expectations change, by this task: its note assertions move to this format and the stored note is read back with ?raw=1 and compared byte for byte with what was sent. A fixture refresh is a lead handover naming the new hivevault commit and sha256, never proofline's own edit.

criteria.statement: for the fixture's inputs the note is byte-identical to the fixture (sha256 held in the test); the path uses the head's sha7; agent.kid equals the envelope's keyid; an L0 receipt yields no note; the PUT body carries raw and no frontmatter object
the fixture from hivevault's writer is committed
the writer no longer sends the frontmatter as an object

tasks.title: The gate's verdict depends only on the pushed commit
tasks.description: Findings of 2026-10-16 (proofline issue 36; hivevault-programme issue 1; the programme solver run, code read on main fe670fb): the pre-push gate is refused for its environment and reads seat-local state. Measured: agentkey 0c30640's sigstore tests fail in the hook's bare worktree under the system temp directory (exit 1, three module-not-found lines) and pass in the same worktree after an install (exit 0). Read in the code: the push worktree and the red-green base worktree get nothing installed (src/index.mjs:326, src/checks.mjs:143), and on the base a missing third-party module reads as red; gateAtCommit takes the base from the seat's own log (index.mjs:320) and the hook reads the working-tree contract (360), falls back to the active file (370) and accepts an untasked push when the log is empty (380-381); approvals are looked up in the temporary worktree, which has no config, so an owner-approved weakening is refused at push (engine.mjs:134); commands inherit the seat's PATH, HOME and TMPDIR. The invariant this task makes true: a push's verdict is a function of (judge commit, pushed commit, base, the contract bytes at the pushed commit, the dependency closure key, node and git versions) and nothing else. 1. Dependencies from the commit: the closure key is sha256 of `git show <sha>:package-lock.json` plus the node version; the closure is built once with `npm ci --ignore-scripts --prefer-offline --no-audit --no-fund` in a staging directory holding only that commit's package.json and package-lock.json, renamed into a shared store (the path comes from the judge configuration, default ~/.proofline/closures), its node_modules made read-only; a second seat reuses it after checking the key. A commit with dependencies and no lockfile is BLOCKED with the command that makes one; a commit with no dependencies gets an empty closure; a network or install failure is BLOCKED, never red. 2. Worktrees under the closure: the push worktree and the red-green base worktree are created under <closure>/w, so node's ancestor lookup finds <closure>/node_modules and nothing is installed inside a worktree; the base worktree uses the head's closure; a bare-specifier module-not-found in the red run is status error, never red. Commands get a fresh TMPDIR outside the closure. 3. Hook mode reads nothing seat-local: contract and task ids come from <sha>:proofline.json; the base is the task's contract base, else a Proofline-Base trailer that is an ancestor, else <sha>^, never the seat's log; no active-file fallback; an untasked push follows defaults.untasked_push ("allow", today's behaviour and the default, or "refuse"); approvals come from the judge configuration's approvals directory. 4. Fixed environment for every command: PATH starts with the directory of the node running proofline, then /usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin; a scratch HOME; LANG=C. 5. Every gate verdict writes a receipt of its inputs (the tuple above plus the decision and the failing test names). 6. Optional gate lock (PROOFLINE_GATE_LOCK=<file>): before any command the hook takes the file exclusively and releases it on exit; if it is held, the hook proceeds only when the holder's token equals PROOFLINE_GATE_TOKEN, else refuses at once and never waits. proofline itself knows nothing of any machine's queue.

criteria.statement: fixture repositories with committed lockfiles and offline file: dependencies: a clean clone's push passes; two clones with different .proofline logs, PATH and HOME give byte-identical input receipts for one commit; a change that adds a dependency reads red on base for behaviour, with no module-not-found counted as red; an owner-approved weakening passes under the hook; dependencies without a lockfile are BLOCKED naming the command; a held gate lock refuses at once

tasks.title: Approvals are owner signatures, armed from the base, never a file the agent can write
tasks.description: Review Critical C2 and High H6. Remove the approvals-directory path from .proofline/config.json and from setup.
